newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. expects to sell first green bonds in March.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. expects to sell first green bonds in March.

text.p: New York State expects to sell in March its first green bonds under the $1.75 billion 1996 Clean Water/Clean Air Act approved by voters in November, a state budget official said on Monday.

The official explained that the current estimate is for the state to sell approximately $50 million of green bonds at the same time that it sells additional general obligation debt for other purposes, such as transportation.
The precise total of the March bond sale has yet to be finalized, as it likely will be changed when Gov. George Pataki releases his new budget along with any revisions.
The state's 1996 fiscal year ends on March 31, and the bond sale that includes the first green bonds would be sold before then.

But this would not be the state's first bond sale in 1997. The New York Assistant Deputy Comptroller last week said the sate planned to sell its first variable rate general obligation debt in a $150 million deal during the first quarter.
The sale is expected to take place in February, the state budget official said.
